name: Surfer (SurferSEO)
summary: Content optimization against live SERP data, and since 2026 a tracker for how often a brand is cited in AI answers like ChatGPT and Google AI Overviews. Billed yearly at four tiers.
best_for: content marketers, SEO specialists and agencies that need on-page optimization against live SERP data and want to start tracking how often they are cited in AI answers
skip_if: you are a solo blogger who needs keyword research rather than document-level optimization, or you cannot commit to a year — every listed rate assumes annual billing
honest_knock: Every tier quotes its monthly rate on annual billing, so the number you see is a year's commitment rather than a monthly one. The meter that actually forces an upgrade is documents: 120 to 360 optimizations depending on tier, which a working content team passes faster than it expects. And the AI-visibility tracking that the product now leads with is capped by prompt count per tier, so watching more of your market costs a step up rather than an add-on.

pricing.plans_source: hand-curated from the vendor's pricing page
pricing.notes:
(re-read 2026-09-19 on surferseo.com/pricing from the Netherlands; earlier reads 2026-08-25 from the Netherlands and 2026-08-26 over a US connection) Billed yearly: Discovery $49/mo, Standard $99/mo, Pro $182/mo and Peace of Mind $299/mo, with Enterprise at $999/mo and AI Search Analytics sold on its own from $82/mo. Monthly billing is on the same cards behind the toggle and is no longer something you have to work out: $59, $119, $219, $359 and $95, with the annual commitment saving between $120 and $720 a year, up to 17 percent by their own FAQ.

AI Search Analytics is a ladder rather than a single price, which is the part that catches people out. Its card carries a prompt dropdown and each step is a complete monthly price: 50 prompts at $82 a month on the annual commitment or $95 monthly, 100 prompts at $158 or $185, 200 prompts at $308 or $365. The tier the card opens on changed on 8 September 2026 from 100 prompts to 50, so a quote of $158 from August and a quote of $82 from today are both correct readings of the same unchanged ladder — they are different rungs. Check which rung your checkout page is on before you compare it with anything.

Worth knowing if you are outside the US: we read this page from both sides and the numbers do not convert. A European is quoted €49 to €299 where an American is quoted $49 to $299, which at today's rate makes the same subscription materially more expensive in Europe.
